capabilities: Highlight the cursor word across all registered editor panes
Propagate highlights from single-line text selections to other panes
Configure matching with case sensitivity, whole words, minimum length and extra word characters
Toggle and clear highlights via commands with assignable hotkeys
disambiguation: Not a text-annotation tool; it only decorates matches visually via CodeMirror and never modifies note contents.
extras: README details limitations (Reading View not highlighted, selection length caps, hidden-tab behavior untested) and an Android selection guard that is on by default but not fully tested across devices. Command IDs changed before first public release, so hotkeys from older builds may need rebinding. Development was assisted by ChatGPT; no network requests or telemetry; MIT license.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to visually track occurrences of the current word or selection across split editor panes and different notes at once.
summary: Editor plugin that highlights the word under the cursor or the selected text across all visible Markdown editor panes, including other notes.
